title: P-IDENTITY: Complete public identity, reservation and capacity contracts
delivery: An application safely creates independent worlds, reserves and materializes entities, grows storage and receives precise exhaustion/refusal results without losing owners.

title: P-FRAGMENTS: Compose typed schema fragments without descriptor collisions
delivery: Two independently authored schema fragments form a usable public world with component, resource, event and service access confined to the composed schema.

title: P-FEATURES: Execute reusable features with declared dependencies
delivery: An application selects reusable features, binds their declared dependencies to its final schema and executes bootstrap/update schedules in authored feature order.

title: P-BUNDLES: Spawn and insert heterogeneous typed component bundles
delivery: A caller authors reusable heterogeneous component bundles and uses them in public spawn/insert commands without consuming payloads on refusal.

title: P-RELATIONS: Maintain directed links and inverse queries through barriers
delivery: Systems create, replace and remove typed directed entity links and query both ends with consistent inverse results.

title: P-RELATION-READERS: Observe deferred relation failures independently
delivery: Registered systems independently consume ordered relation mutation failures without conflating them with system transaction failure.

title: P-HIERARCHY: Preserve ordered traversal, cycle rejection and linked cleanup
delivery: An application reparents an ordered hierarchy, traverses it and removes linked subtrees with exact cleanup and diagnostics.

title: P-SCOPES: Clean entity lifetime groups while preserving persistent entities
delivery: A scene-style lifetime scope owns a group of spawned entities and queues cleanup without deleting persistent entities.

title: P-DECODE: Validate constructed and transient descriptor boundaries
delivery: Applications construct components/resources from typed raw input and receive exact failures before invalid values or partial work enter the world.

title: P-COMPONENT-STATE: Execute typed finite component states
delivery: Systems author finite-valued state components, query them and update them transactionally using typed values.

title: P-MACHINES: Queue and apply global state transitions with conditions
delivery: An application declares finite machines, reads committed states, queues changes and gates schedules by machine conditions at explicit transition markers.

title: P-TRANSITION-HANDLERS: Preserve exit, transition and enter failure boundaries
delivery: Applications attach typed exit/transition/enter schedules and retry failed transitions without undoing already committed work.

title: P-CAPTURES: Repeatedly execute systems with owned runtime capture state
delivery: Independently authored systems retain runtime affine capture state across repeated registration, execution, failure and disposal.

title: P-CAPTURE-SCHEDULES: Compose heterogeneous captured system instances
delivery: An application reuses typed heterogeneous captured systems across nested schedules with safe registration, disposal and refusal.

title: P-RECOVERY: Restore general affine payload operations through explicit inverses
delivery: Systems perform recoverable operations on caller-owned affine component/resource payloads and preserve exact state after failed ECS transactions.

title: P-AFFINE-EVENTS: Publish and read owned event payloads without illicit copies
delivery: Event publishers and multiple independent readers use useful affine Type payloads under an explicit ownership-safe publication and projection contract.

title: P-INSPECT: Read public world projections without consuming system visibility
delivery: Host code repeatedly inspects components, resources and event/removal streams while leaving system reader positions and retention unchanged.

title: P-INSPECT-GRAPH: Inspect relations, machines and failure streams safely
delivery: Read-only inspectors observe hierarchy, machine states, transition events and relation failures without affecting schedules or readers.

title: P-DEBUG-DESCRIBE: Describe and dump public ECS structure without side effects
delivery: A developer enables schema/system/schedule descriptions, lints, access indexes and filtered world dumps without changing ECS behavior.

title: P-DEBUG-TRACE: Observe execution, failure and barrier traces with disposal
delivery: A developer subscribes to ordered execution observations and unsubscribes/resets them without interfering with ECS execution.

title: P-SAVE: Export validated basic world snapshots with independent payload data
delivery: An application exports basic entities, components, resources and allocator progress into an independent save value while preserving the live world.

title: P-RESTORE: Validate and atomically restore basic saved worlds
delivery: An application loads a basic save, rejects invalid input before mutation and resumes normal entity/lifecycle operations.

title: P-RESTORE-GRAPH: Save and restore ordered relations and committed machines
delivery: A complete public save restores ordered relation graphs and committed machine values with the exact runtime omissions and stream-clearing boundary.

title: P-PARITY-AUDIT: Execute the complete pinned core capability matrix
delivery: An independent public consumer verifies the whole pinned core surface and reports exact remaining differences before full parity is claimed.

title: P-LAWS-PLAN: Draft and falsify remaining exact core laws
delivery: Maintainers receive a source-bound set of precise remaining laws with falsification evidence and explicit approval status.

title: P-SIMULATION: Execute the complete deterministic fixed-step ECS scenario
delivery: A reproducible console simulation spawns entities, moves them toward a goal, applies damage, removes them and reports hit/death events through the public ECS API.

title: P-DEFENSE-PLAN: Freeze copied Tower Defense integration requirements
delivery: A concrete integration plan identifies the exact ECS contracts needed by a separate copy of Canonical Tower Defense without modifying its original repository.
